name: Kalooki (Caribbean)
description: Kalooki (specifically the Caribbean or Jamaican version) is a high-stakes, 108-card contract rummy game. Played over nine rounds with increasing difficulty, it requires players to complete specific 'contracts' of sets (threes) and runs (fours). It is a central part of Caribbean social life and is known for the 'Call' mechanic where players can snatch discards out of turn.

history.origins: Derived from European Rummy games (like Kalooki 40), it was heavily adapted in Jamaica to include the 'out-of-turn call' and specific contract escalations.
timeline: Early 20th Century: European immigrants bring Rummy variants to the Caribbean.
1950s: Modern Jamaican Kalooki rules emerge in Kingston social clubs.
1980s: Becomes a popular competitive game in the UK and USA alongside the Jamaican diaspora.
Present: A cultural icon of Jamaican gaming, played in professional tournaments and family gatherings.
history.cultural: In Jamaica, Kalooki is synonymous with social focus; 'calling' a card (taking a discard out of turn) is an aggressive and strategic social move.
history.evolution: The game's length (9 rounds) and high card count (up to 16 cards per hand) make it one of the most endurance-based Rummy variants.

setup.deck: Two standard decks and four Jokers (Total 108 cards).
setup.dealing: Varies by round: Hand 1 (9 cards), Hand 2 (10), ... Hand 9 (16 cards).
setup.equipment: 108 cards, score sheet, chips for stakes (optional)

rules.objective: Be the first to 'Go Out' by melding all cards in your hand and have the lowest total score after 9 hands.
rules.gameplay:
1. **Contracts**: Each hand has a specific contract to fulfill before melding.
2. **The Call**: Any player can call for a discard out of turn. If accepted, they must take the discard PLUS a penalty card from the stock. (Limit: 3 calls per hand).
3. **Melds**: Threes (sets) and Fours (runs). Jokers are wild.
4. **Pointing**: Jokers (25), Black Aces (15), K-Q-J-10 (10), 2-9 (Face), Red Aces (1). Lowest total wins.
keyRules: The Call: Take discard out of turn with penalty card (max 3 calls)
Jokers are wild but cannot be consecutive in a run
Must have at least two natural cards in a set

strategy.basic: Don't 'Call' cards in the early rounds unless it completes your Eye/Set. The penalty cards accumulate fast and can leave you with too many points if you don't go out first.
strategy.intermediate: Watch the 'Aces'. Black Aces (15) are dangerous to hold, but Red Aces (1) are excellent for lowering your point total if you are caught with cards at the end.
strategy.advanced: The 'Bending' Rule: If you go 'Down and Out' (meld your entire hand in one turn), your opponents score double points for their remaining cards. Try to time your melds to achieve this.
tips: Count the Jokers! If 3 are on the table, the 4th is a high-value target to call.
In the 16-card final round, hoarding low-value cards (2, 3, 4) is better than chasing high-value sets.
